chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Khalid ibn Jarir from Abu al-Rabii said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who lent a man dirhams, and he returned to him better quality ones with a good spirit, and the borrower and the lender knew that he only lent it so that he would give him better quality ones. He said: 'There is no harm if the borrower is pleased with it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to repay a loan with higher quality currency than what was borrowed?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the key condition for validity is the borrower's voluntary satisfaction (tawaffun nafs), distinguishing this from riba al-fadl where excess is obligatory. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on mutual consent and the absence of coercion in financial transactions, ensuring that the 'better quality' given is a gift of goodwill rather than a fixed debt component.
